summary: Both sides draw the same completely static 6-band pride flag with identical band order, widths and index mapping, but the port replaces the original's exact official flag hex colours with full-saturation/full-value hue approximations (neon green and neon magenta instead of deep green #008026 and violet #750787) and omits the 1-px black band separators the original draws on any strip whose length is divisible by 6.
observations: Both sides are COMPLETELY STATIC. motion 0 and motionLit 0 on every captured frame, zeroMotionFrames = 120/120 at 6 s/20 fps, 300/300 at 60 s/5 fps, 480/480 at 240 s/2 fps, and 200/200 in a late window (--skip 300 --seconds 10 --fps 20). brightnessTrend 'steady' on both. Frame dumps at t=0 and t=3 s are byte-identical on both sides. There is exactly one regime; no mode rotation, no drift, no slow palette walk.

Both sides are index-driven and rig-independent: renders at --pixels 12/30/60/61/64/66/120/300, --seed 1234, and --wall-clock 1700000000 all produce byte-identical output to the default run on their respective rigs, and on --rig grid --grid 16x16 both sides paint the bands across rows in flat-index order (rows uniform, boundaries at the same rows on both sides: transitions inside rows 2, 5, 10, 13 on BOTH sides). Structural mapping matches exactly.

Band order matches exactly on both sides: violet at pixel 0 -> blue -> green -> yellow -> orange -> red at pixel 59 (i.e. the flag drawn reversed, red at the far end). Band widths on the default 60-px strip: orig 10/9/9/9/9/9 px separated by 1 black px; port 10/10/10/10/10/10 px with no separators.

ORIGINAL PALETTE (exact --dump RGB, 60-px strip): violet [117,7,135] = #750787; blue [0,76,255] ~ #004DFF; green [0,127,35] ~ #008026; yellow [255,237,0] = #FFED00; orange [255,140,0] = #FF8C00; red [226,2,2] ~ #E40303. These are the six official 2018 pride-flag hex values, reproduced essentially exactly (within 1-2 counts of quantisation).

PORT PALETTE (same dump): violet [203,0,255]; blue [0,71,255]; green [5,255,0]; yellow [255,244,0]; orange [255,107,0]; red [255,0,0]. Every entry is at (or within 2% of) full HSV saturation AND full value - the port looks like hsv(h,1,1) over an approximate hue table rather than the flag's literal hex colours.

Per-band RGB distance orig->port: violet 148 (worst), green 133 (second worst), orange 33, red 29, yellow 7, blue 5. So four of six bands are visually fine; VIOLET and GREEN are the two that read wrong - the original's deep aubergine purple becomes neon magenta and the original's forest green becomes neon lime.

Hue angles (0..1) orig vs port: violet 0.810/0.799, blue 0.616/0.620, green 0.383/0.330, yellow 0.155/0.160, orange 0.0915/0.070, red 0.002/0.000. Hue is close on four bands; the port's GREEN hue is 0.053 too low (pure green instead of the flag's slightly cyan-leaning green) and its ORANGE hue is 0.022 too low (too red). The bigger error on violet and green is VALUE/SATURATION, not hue: orig violet V=0.53, port V=1.00; orig green V=0.50, port V=1.00.

Mean brightness over the whole window: orig 95, port 120 (+26%). Channel means orig R130 G88 B66 vs port R162 G113 B85. The port is uniformly brighter because it maxes value on every band and has no black separator pixels.

BLACK SEPARATORS: the original inserts one fully black pixel (0,0,0) at each of the 5 internal band boundaries whenever the strip length is divisible by 6 - confirmed at 12 px (idx 2,4,6,8,10), 30 px (5,10,15,20,25), 60 px (10,20,30,40,50), 66 px (11,22,33,44,55), 120 px (20,40,60,80,100), 300 px (50,100,150,200,250). At 61 px, 64 px and on the 256-px grid the original has NO black pixels, so this is a boundary/rounding artefact of the original's band math rather than a deliberately-sized gap - but on the default 60-px rig (and on every typical 6-divisible strip) it is plainly visible as thin black rules between the bands. The port never produces one at any pixel count tested.

Neither side exposes ANY controls: meta.json sides.orig.controls and sides.port.controls are both empty, and --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for both. Control surfaces match. No dialed comparison is applicable.
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both), so the run is unaffected by the synthetic feed; no compile or runtime errors on either side in any run.
feedback: Palette is the main fix. The original uses the literal official 2018 pride-flag hex values, not hue-wheel colours: red #E40303 (226,2,2 as rendered), orange #FF8C00 (255,140,0), yellow #FFED00 (255,237,0), green #008026 (0,127,35), blue #004DFF (0,76,255), violet #750787 (117,7,135). The port should emit those RGB triples directly instead of deriving hsv(h,1,1) from a hue table.

The two bands that actually read as wrong to a viewer are VIOLET and GREEN, and the error is brightness/saturation, not hue: the port draws violet [203,0,255] where the original draws [117,7,135] (roughly half the value), and green [5,255,0] where the original draws [0,127,35] (again roughly half the value, and slightly too far from cyan). Fixing just these two bands recovers most of the flag's character.

Two smaller colour nits once the above is done: the port's orange [255,107,0] is too red - it should be [255,140,0]; and the port's red [255,0,0] should be the flag's slightly-darker [226,2,2]/#E40303. The port's blue and yellow are already correct within 7 counts.

Reproduce the original's 1-px black separator at each internal band boundary. The original blanks the pixel that sits exactly on a boundary, which manifests only when the pixel count divides evenly by 6 (verified: separators present at 12/30/60/66/120/300 px, absent at 61/64/256 px, always at indices k*(n/6) for k=1..5 and never at index 0). Whatever band-index expression produces that edge case on the original, the port should reproduce it - it is visible on the default 60-px rig as thin black rules and it accounts for part of the +26% mean-brightness gap.

No timing, motion, structural or control work is needed: band order (violet at index 0 through red at the last pixel), band widths, flat-index mapping, rig/pixel-count independence, seed independence, wall-clock independence and the fully-static character already match the original exactly.
